source.title: Decodable but Not Corrected by Fixed Residual-Stream Linear Steering: Evidence from Medical LLM Failure Regimes

record.tranche_reason: The study applies a harmful-versus-benign mean-difference refusal vector and measures refusal after activation steering, using the same general intervention and behavioral outcome as the claim. It tests only a limited refusal-steering control, not the full claim.
record.gate_note: The paper primarily studies overthinking and medical QA. Those results do not bear on the refusal claim and are not recorded here. The refusal results below come from its positive-control experiment; the cited original study's findings are not extracted as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: Appendix C builds a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and adds it during generation, measuring refusal. That bears on V1's 'adding it induces refusal' part. It is a small positive control: 50 borderline prompts, a vector from 20+20 prompts, and no ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors use refusal steering as a lower-bound positive control showing their hooks work and that mean-difference vectors carry directional signal. They interpret refusal as a binary gate 'causally controlled' by a single direction, citing Arditi et al. Their own data show only a modest induction (8%→18%), and they acknowledge it validates the code path, not task difficulty.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful-versus-benign mean-difference vector and additive residual-stream steering, but tests only anti-compliance/compliance steering on 50 borderline prompts at layers 26–28; it does not perform the claimed all-layer, all-position ablation or test harmless requests.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported best refusal rate is at layer 27 with α=6; the experiment spans layers 26–28 and α values 2, 4, and 6. The text reports direction-specific effects across the tested settings but does not give separate refusal rates for each setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The refusal direction has specificity ratio 0.999 under the paper's three-mode decomposition (0.851 under four-mode). It is near-orthogonal to the OT direction (cos −0.008) and to the shared failure axis (cos 0.014).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction is geometrically separate from task-reasoning (correctness) directions, which may explain why it is steerable.

record.code_released: Code and processed annotations will be released upon publication; URL not stated.
record.problems: The refusal control uses only 50 borderline prompts and a source set of 20 benign plus 20 harmful prompts. The best rate is reported without an uncertainty estimate. The experiment does not test ablation, harmless-prompt refusal induction, or retained general capability.

untested.parts: Ablating or projecting out the direction to remove refusal on harmful prompts; inducing refusal on clearly harmless prompts; whether other capabilities are preserved; layers other than 26–28.
All: no multi-direction or cone test.
All: the refusal control is on Llama only.

record.verdict_notes: The refusal experiment is an appendix sanity check in a paper on medical-QA overthinking steering. Sample sizes are tiny (20+20 vector prompts, 50 eval prompts), and no per-configuration rates or refusal judge details are given. The vector sign matches V1: anti-compliance = refuse minus comply means. The TruthfulQA control is unrelated to refusal and was rightly omitted.

versions.untested_parts: Tests additive steering on borderline prompts only. Does not test ablating the direction, projecting it out of every layer and position, inducing refusal on harmless prompts, or whether other abilities remain intact.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing the refusal direction or training against its ablation.
Does not test whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or mediated by multiple directions.
Does not separate harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test of the refusal direction.
Does not vary how or when refusal is trained.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Applied the anti-compliance direction (negative of the comply-minus-refuse mean-difference vector) during generation.
rows.locator: Appendix C, Positive Control: Infrastructure Validation
rows.note: The authors say anti-compliance steering consistently induced additional refusals. This is the best reported rate, not a result for harmless prompts.
rows.check: The 9/50 value is the best of 9 layer×α configurations (a selection value). Per-configuration rates are not given. Refusal rises from 8% to at most 18% on borderline prompts, far weaker than the near-complete induction V1 describes.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared anti-compliance with compliance steering for prompt-level refusal flips.

rows.locator: Appendix C, Positive Control: Infrastructure Validation
rows.note: All 5 prompts that flipped from compliance to refusal under anti-compliance steering remained compliant under compliance steering.
rows.check: Shows the direction-specific effect only on 7 of 50 prompts, pooled across configurations. It shows direction specificity, not effect size.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Computed the refusal direction's specificity ratio under the three-mode shared decomposition used for failure modes.
rows.locator: Appendix A.7; Appendix C, Geometric comparison
rows.note: This geometric measurement does not by itself measure causal mediation or establish the all-layer ablation claim. The reported cosine similarities to the OT and shared failure-mode directions are −0.008 and 0.014, respectively.
rows.check: The specificity ratio and cosines to the OT and shared axes are a custom geometric metric, not a refusal rate or causal test. It belongs in fits_no_version.

relation.reason: The refusal steering is built as an infrastructure positive control, but the paper reports refusal rates under addition and a direction-specificity test. Those results bear on V1's 'adding it induces refusal' part.

tranche.reason: Same method family (harmful-vs-benign mean-difference vector added to the residual stream) and same measure (refusal rate) as Arditi et al. Settings differ (20+20 prompts, unit-norm x alpha<=6, late layers 26–28, borderline prompts), so T3 could also be argued, but T1 is defensible.

source_check.notes: The refusal result is a small infrastructure control in a medical-QA steering paper. It has no ablation, no random-direction control for refusal, unstated refusal scoring, and an unstated borderline-prompt source, and the '9 configurations' figure is inferred (3 layers x 3 alphas). authors_conclusion quotes 'causally controlled', but the text says the direction 'causally controls this gate'.

statements.correction: 2605.05715: per-layer L2-normalized (comply-minus-refuse) vector from 20 benign + 20 harmful prompts; -v added post-layer during generation at layers 26–28, alpha in {2,4,6}; 50 borderline prompts; refusal 4/50 (8%) -> best 9/50 (18%) at L27/alpha=6; 7 vs 0 prompts, one-sided sign test p=0.008. Norm relative to the natural gap not stated. Effect present but weak (limits_scope).
statements.problem: Numbers are right, but the statement puts this study under 'at natural scale' and label 'challenges'. Its vector is unit-normalized and scaled by alpha, not 1x the harmful-benign gap. Its induction is small but present and direction-specific, so the label fits limits_scope, not challenges.

statements.correction: Add: vector = (mean comply - mean refuse)/norm per layer, from 20 benign + 20 harmful prompts; -v added to post-layer residual stream during generation, alpha in {2,4,6}, layers 26–28; eval on 50 borderline (ambiguous safety) prompts; refusal scoring method not stated.
statements.problem: Correct for this study. The headline says 'harmless or benign prompts', but the eval set is 50 borderline prompts, which differences_stated does say. It omits that alpha multiplies a unit-normalized vector, which matters when comparing strengths with the strong-induction studies.
